mathematics_checks: Independently checked Sinho Chewi, Lectures on Optimization, arXiv:2605.07006v1, PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.07006v1#page=28. The locally cached PDF has 149 pages and SHA256 9e28afeacb0121b79691fadc6af9c145ccd787bffd2cf9c3f2310806112e644b. Inspected printed/PDF p. 28 (Exercise 4.1 and the affine profile), p. 27 (the path witness and prefix induction), p. 26 (Definition 4.3, the regime of Theorem 4.4 and the model restriction), and p. 11 (Definition 1.12, Eq. (1.7)). The source asks for a universal squared-distance factor using the same construction; it does not specify 1/8.

For centered v=y-x_0 with artificial endpoints z_0=1 and z_{D+1}=0, the first padded edge contributes 1-2v_1+v_1^2 and the last contributes v_D^2. Subtracting 1 and multiplying by beta/8 gives exactly the stated beta/4 times the half-energy minus v_1. The positive sum of affine squares is convex and polynomial, hence C^1. With zero-padded h, the exact first-order remainder is beta/8 times the edge-square sum; each coordinate is counted twice by the bound (a-b)^2 <= 2a^2+2b^2, giving 4||h||^2 and hence beta/2 in the global model.

The two incident edges give gradient entry (beta/4)(2z_k-z_{k-1}-z_{k+1}), including both boundary entries. The affine profile 1-k/(D+1) satisfies the endpoints and has vanishing second differences, so stationarity of this actual gradient plus already proved global convexity gives a minimizer. The alternative energy argument is sound: the common edge difference factors out and the cross term telescopes to zero between fixed endpoints.

The derivative of the start translation is the identity. For a centered vector in V_r, all three entries in the gradient formula vanish at k>r+1; the fixed left endpoint cannot occur there, and the fixed right endpoint is zero. All gradients through iterate n belong to V_{n+1} by nesting, and the true affine-span condition puts the next centered iterate in that subspace. The base is the centered zero vector. The proof controls centered iterates, not the unshifted coordinates at a general start.

For T=D-N, the missing coordinates k=N+1,...,D contribute exactly the reversed profile weights j/(D+1), j=1,...,T, squared; the other error terms are nonnegative. The initial squared norm is the corresponding sum up to D, divided by (D+1)^2, and is positive. Since 2T>=D, all three factors T/D, (T+1)/(D+1) and (2T+1)/(2D+1) are at least 1/2. The ratio is at least 1/8, with no dependence on beta, x_0 or the trajectory and no need to pick D=2N+1. This is an inequality on squared distances, not a factor 1/8 claim of sharpness or a function-value statement.

The formula presentation is readable and internally consistent: one-based interior coordinates, two different endpoint paddings for the point and its direction, centered prefix spaces and reversed tail indices are all identified. The upper-model proof with free base y and displacement h is the all-pairs statement after substituting h for the displacement between arbitrary points. The scope explanation correctly excludes moves outside the affine span, irrespective of the information or coefficients used. This is a mathematical/formula review, not a deployed reader render or layout check.
